beats.intent: ThinkSR keeps a dense carrier while a compact thought process repeatedly reads and updates it before decoding.
beats.claim: A persistent dense carrier, read and updated by a compact thought process.
beats.narration: ThinkSR separates the spatial field from the recurrent thought that acts on it. The encoder turns the low-resolution image into features. Windowing organizes the dense field for local processing. The DQ-CTM thought process reads and updates those window tokens across ticks. The decoder maps the updated dense field back to a super-resolution image. The recurrence returns to the thought stage itself, with parameters shared across ticks.

beats.intent: The carrier equation first builds a dense feature field, then partitions that field into windows without dropping tokens.
beats.narration: The carrier is defined before the recurrent thought process begins. The feature field is the persistent dense representation. The encoder maps the low-resolution input into that field. The window tokens are the objects passed forward for processing. The window partition is applied to the dense field, so every token comes from the carrier.

params.headline: The dense carrier is encoded first, then partitioned into windows.

beats.intent: DQ-CTM-SR is not the cheapest method in the benchmark; its 1.129 million parameters are second largest among the five listed methods.
beats.claim: Table 1 reports parameters: CATANet 0.535M, RFDN 0.550M, IMDN 0.715M, DQ-CTM-SR 1.129M, CARN 1.592M.
beats.narration: The parameter comparison keeps the methods in ascending order, so smaller models appear before larger ones. CATANet has the fewest parameters in this table. RFDN and IMDN remain under one million parameters. DQ-CTM-SR has one point one two nine million parameters, making it the second largest of the five. CARN is larger still at one point five nine two million parameters.
